events.title: Congo Free State
hints: A private colony run by a European king as a personal business venture.
Villages faced harsh rubber quotas enforced by violence.
International outrage forced the king to hand it over to his own government in 1908.
events.summary: King Leopold II of Belgium ruled the territory as a personal possession from 1885, extracting ivory and wild rubber through forced labour and violence. Estimates of the death toll run into the millions. International protest forced him to cede it to the Belgian state in 1908.

events.title: Belgian Congo
hints: A colony run by a small European monarchy whose mines supplied two world wars.
Its Shinkolobwe mine supplied uranium for the first atomic bombs.
Independence arrived in 1960 and a crisis began within days.
events.summary: After taking over from Leopold II in 1908, Belgium administered the colony through the state, the Church and large companies such as Union Minière. Copper, diamonds, gold, tin and uranium flowed out. Independence came in June 1960.
events.quip: A country smaller than several of its colony's provinces ran the place with remarkable administrative confidence.

events.title: Katanga secession backed by Belgian interests
hints: A mineral-rich province declared itself independent just days after the country did.
Foreign mining interests and some troops from the former colonial power backed the breakaway.
events.summary: In July 1960 the copper-rich province of Katanga seceded under Moïse Tshombe. Belgian troops and mining interests, notably Union Minière, supported the breakaway state until UN forces ended it in January 1963.
